_: Template standard shared by both builders. One art ratio, everywhere.

art.label: plate
art.why: A 4:5 page subdivides into n x n cells that are also 4:5 (drift <1%). No other subdivision of a 4:5 page holds the ratio, so 1, 4 or 9 panels per page is the whole grammar. One ratio means every render drops into any slot with no crop and no per-panel size bookkeeping.
art.why_this_size: 2432x3040 is the largest exact 4:5 whose edges are both multiples of 16 (64n x 80n, n=38) and which clears 300dpi on the 8x10in trim: 304dpi both axes. 1920x2400, the old plate, was 240dpi -- fine on screen, short for print.

print.why: 8x10in is 4:5, so the trim, the page and the plate are all the same shape and a splash is full-bleed with zero crop. Bleed is cut off the plate, not added to it -- a 2432x3040 render already carries 38px of slop per edge at 304dpi.

targets.why: Phone is out of scope. At 402px a grid4 cell is 181px wide and a caption box covers half of it; the fixes all amount to a different reader (guided view, one panel at a time), not a CSS tweak. Tablet portrait (768px) is the floor both builders are tuned against.

reference_policy: Likeness across panels comes from attaching a canonical reference render, not from re-describing the character. Generate each sheet once, keep it forever, attach it to every prompt that names its subject. See docs/likeness.md.
fixed_marks: the band is on the LEFT wrist, always
Walt's sleeves are rolled, and the rig is on his belt, not a shoulder strap
the visitor has TWO ridges at the throat, not three
fixed_marks_why: Faces are hard to compare by eye; asymmetries are easy. These are the checkable fingerprints -- they cost one clause in the prompt and turn 'does this look like him?' into a yes/no check on delivery.

exceptions.6c: band 9.96:1 — delivered as a painted letterbox; page reshaped to suit it
exceptions.10a: band 4.72:1 — delivered as a painted letterbox; page reshaped to suit it

exception_policy: Bands are grandfathered where the art already exists and earns it. New art is 4:5. tools/art-orders.py warns on any slot outside tolerance that is not listed here.
